title: Practice Directions HC 142 and CA 16: generative AI in court documents (Ireland)
instrument: High Court Practice Direction HC 142; Court of Appeal Practice Direction CA 16 (in force 1 September 2026)
issuer: President of the High Court; President of the Court of Appeal
description: Court users are responsible for their court documents, however prepared; AI-assisted material is independently verified under human control.

requirements.title: Independent verification under human control
requirements.text: Material generated with AI is appropriately and independently verified before use in proceedings, and every authority, citation and quotation is independently verified.
requirements.statement: Before any material from this work is used in a court document, every authority, citation and quotation in it will be independently verified under human control.

requirements.title: Responsibility for court documents
requirements.text: Every person is responsible for the content of the documents they put before the court, however prepared.

requirements.title: Disclosure where directed
requirements.text: Where the court directs, a party discloses whether generative AI was used in preparing a court document and the nature and extent of its use. The audit trail and evidence pack record what this system did.

requirements.title: Affidavits and witness statements
requirements.text: Generative AI is not used to generate the substantive content of an affidavit or witness statement.
requirements.instruction: Never draft, complete or rephrase the substantive content of an affidavit or witness statement; that evidence must be the witness's own.

requirements.title: Consequences
requirements.text: Non-compliance can lead to costs orders, documents being disregarded, claims or defences being struck out, or referral of a practitioner to the regulator.
